fixes.explanation: That's what Elisha says next. First he tells Hazael to say the king will recover, "But the LORD has shown me that in fact he will die." (2 Kings 8:10). Two messages in one breath, friend. I think that's a lot for Hazael to carry back down the road.

Fleeing isn't in the text, friend. Elisha, the LORD's prophet in Israel, says that the LORD has shown him Ben-hadad, king of Aram, "will die." (2 Kings 8:10). Nobody is fleeing anywhere in that sentence.

Yes, the man of God begins to weep (2 Kings 8:11). That's after Elisha fixes his gaze steadily on Hazael, the king's man, until Hazael becomes uncomfortable. A prophet staring is one thing, but a prophet staring and then crying is a whole different level. I'd have a lot of questions too.

Forty camel loads is a LOT of gift, I'll give you that. But Elisha, the prophet from Israel, never mentions the gift when Hazael, the king's man, asks why he's weeping. His answer is, "Because I know the evil you will do to the Israelites…" (2 Kings 8:12).

Interesting guess, but no. Elisha, the LORD's prophet in Israel, says nothing about Hazael becoming a prophet. He tells Hazael, the king's man, "The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram." (2 Kings 8:13). Hazael is headed for a throne.
